sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the Adriatic sector offshore the town of Roseto degli Abruzzi and roughly follows the Vomano River onshore, representing the northernmost expression of the oblique to right-lateral strike-slip system that affects the central and southern Adriatic foreland. This high-angle, SE dipping Source splits the Pescara Basin in two sectors; the northern one hosts the more advanced thrust front of the Central Apennines, whereas the southern one is a relatively undisturbed monocline.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (ISIDe Working Group, 2007; Guidoboni et al., 2019; Rovida et al., 2021) show scarce seismicity in this region, for instance like the 10 January 1884, Mw 4.6 Atri earthquake.
This Source is a blind strike-slip, right-lateral fault system that is thought to run ca. ENE-WSW across the northernmost sector of the Apulian domain. The fault is recognized in seismic reflection profiles (Bolis et al., 2003) as a discontinuity mapped within the carbonate succession of the Adriatic foreland up to the Messinian unconformity.
The fault does not propagate within the Plio-Pleistocene succession, where nonetheless reflectors are slightly folded because of the fault activity, suggesting a transpressive kinematics.
South of this Composite Source, the Plio-Pleistocene succession of the Pescara Basin was tilted toward east during the Pleistocene (Del Ben and Oggioni, 2016), whereas the northern sector is characterized by various anticline culminations controlled by thrusts.
This Composite Source is interpreted as the eastern portion of the southern boundary of the Central-Northern Apennines basal decollement.
